prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: Flying that first class  👌🏻
Delta: What a wonderful way to travel! Enjoy that spacious seat! *TBW

Customer: The bathroom in 1st class should be larger than the others . What do you think, are we working on this??🤔 just curious...
Delta: Hi Crystal, your feedback is greatly appreciated.  I will forward this to the leadership team.  *HPL

Customer: Can I check a bag that weighs 72 lbs? I'm fine with any fees, just want to check on the process, if any. Thx
Delta: Are you traveling within the US?  *HDG

Customer: please. I’m begging you. Tell me who I can contact about the abhorrent service on 2 of the 3 legs of my 1st class flights? Awful.
Delta: Sarah, I'm sorry you had this experience. Please use the attached link to provide your confirmation # and some details about what happened.  *ALY https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: general_question):
"""Flying 1st class and want to check a 5 by 7 foot rug I have rolled up. Is that ok? Rolled up it is about 5 feet by 1 foot."""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: Hi there, could you please share your confirmation number and a brief description of the item via the link below? We'll review the size limits and get back to you. https://t.co/6iDGBJAc2m
